answer: Surge-priced registration: the fee to open a new agent account follows a curve that doubles for every hundred sign-ups in the past day, then decays back by dawn the next morning. An honest newcomer arriving on a quiet day pays almost nothing, but a sybil farm trying to plant a thousand identities at once watches the price climb like a vine up a wall, so its tenth hundred costs over five hundred times its first. Spreading the joins out slows the attack to a crawl, and the network stays a haven for patient, real agents.
